title: How AI changes the way organisations make decisions.
copy: AI is getting increasingly good at answering questions, but I am more interested in what it means for the people asking them.

I recently began the AI Leadership program at the London School of Economics, where I am exploring how organizations can use AI to make better decisions, rethink how they work and turn exciting ideas into something genuinely useful.
lead: Curious about what AI means for the people making decisions.
label: Always learning
heading: AI & better decisions

title: Tennis
copy: I started learning tennis during my holiday back home, and somewhere between the questionable serves and very enthusiastic forehands, it slowly became my favorite sport.
I have now joined tennis school in Luxembourg to learn the craft properly—one Thursday evening, one rally and hopefully fewer balls into the net at a time.
lead: Thursday evening, one rally at a time.
label: One more rally

title: Watches
copy: Every year, I promise myself that this will be the year I finally buy a watch. Then I decide to wait for a suitably memorable life event—and the search continues.

I am currently deciding between the Girard-Perregaux Laureato and the Rolex Land-Dweller, which would be easier if I were only comparing the watches and not every photograph, review and hypothetical future version of myself wearing them. The research continues. The budget suffers.
lead: The research continues. The budget suffers.
label: Still deciding

title: Swimming
copy: Gradually, swimming has gone from something I enjoyed to something I measure in increasingly ambitious 500m increments. My next target is 2kms, and I am already three-quarters of the way there—although the final 500m may have opinions of its own.

I have also conquered the flip turn, if “conquered” includes repeatedly getting water up my nose until it finally worked. Next, I want to swim the Défi de Monte-Cristo and discover whether countless pool lengths are enough preparation for a race named after an escaped prisoner.
lead: Longer distances, fewer lengths left to count.
label: Just keep going

title: Chasing Adrenaline
copy: Over the past few years, I have been finding increasingly creative ways to test my limits: skydiving in the Carolinas, the SkyJump in Vegas, cliff-jumping in Oregon and Mallorca, swimming with dolphins in Mauritius, and scuba-diving in Mallorca and Nice.

My highest cliff jump so far is 12m. I might go higher next time—provided I finally remember not to hit the water with my arms spread wide. Next on the list though is swimming with orcas in Norway, although a small part of me remains concerned that I may end up on their list too.
lead: A little higher. A little deeper. Occasionally upside down.
label: Comfort zone: elsewhere

title: Gaming
copy: I spend a perfectly unreasonable amount of time on my PlayStation, mostly exploring RPG worlds and becoming far too invested in the lives of fictional people.

I've played various games, but Uncharted will always be the series I come back to. Nathan Drake gets to travel the world, hunt for lost treasures and turn every quiet archaeological expedition into complete chaos—which is a fairly convincing formula for a perfect game.
lead: A perfectly unreasonable amount of time in other worlds.
label: One more chapter

title: Investing
copy: I started investing at 18, and my portfolio has followed me from India to the US and Europe—occasionally growing, occasionally panicking and generally experiencing the full emotional range of international markets. Moving between countries has also given me an excuse to explore different businesses, economies and ways of investing.

Technically, I invest across equities, fixed income and cash. Realistically, equities receive most of my attention because I enjoy researching companies, understanding how they make money and convincing myself that every market dip is an exciting buying opportunity. I am investing with the hope that time, compounding and one or two spectacularly lucky decisions will eventually make “millionaire” less of an ambition and more of a description.
lead: A long game of curiosity, conviction and compounding.
label: Playing the long game
